141 Six more Explore screens

Six more whole screens, each built on something Astute is for. 141a keeps asking why: every answer opens the next question, until it clicks. 141b gives cards with nothing to answer a reaction of their own: swipe a fact right if it was new to you, left if you knew it. 141c travels through time on a ruler of years, from the first light to today’s shelf. 141d asks where you stand before a card and again after it, so a change of mind can be counted. 141e turns cards into lines to say at dinner, the “said” that Top of the week already counts. 141f lays the day out as a front page. All six are live, and none of these features is in the app yet. The facts, chains and claims are written for the prototype and can be checked.

140 Whole Explore screens, one idea each

Five Explore screens, each built on one line of SCOPO.md. 140a the expert who appears between the cat videos and explains a why: pick an expert and see the question they always ask. 140b cards made for you, in every tone: pick a mood and the minutes you have. 140c connecting the dots: every card sits where two subjects meet. 140d a day is a mix of reading and doing, and some things take a few cards: a sixty-second round, then short series. 140e finding again the questions you asked: search every card, and see the questions you typed with the cards that answered them. Each screen starts under the search and the subject chips. Today’s shelf and Top of the week are left out so the idea reads on its own. All five are live, and most add something the app doesn’t do yet.

139 Bet: estimate it before you open it

SCOPO.md lists a bet and a slider to move among the ways a card can tell its story. Here the bet becomes a shelf, for percentages and for plain numbers. Every answer can be checked: some are worked out on the card (the 30-day streak, the positive test, the shared birthday, the two dice), the others name the study they come from. Each version bets in a different way and adds one more idea next to it. Everything above the shelves stays as in 131a. 139a bet a range, narrow or wide, with a bet slip. 139b stake points from a daily 100, and send a bet to a friend. 139c set a number with steppers, and pick the bigger of two figures. 139d close in with three steps of more or less, and guess orders of magnitude. 139e the bet of the day, then what everyone else guessed. The crowd figures in 139e are made up for the prototype.

138 The bottom of Explore: six more directions

SCOPO.md lists what should happen to someone who uses Astute: they feel “ah, that’s why”, they see the trick in a headline, an offer or an argument, they ask better questions about their own life, and they can see that they are changing. Each version turns one of those into the shelves under “The ones that ask the most”, and each ends the page in its own way. Everything above stays as in 131a. 138a shelves by the feeling a card gives. 138b by where the trick hides. 138c by the questions to ask about your own life. 138d cards you play on the shelf: a slider, a trick to spot, a chart to unmask. 138e every shelf as a set to finish, where reading counts as much as answering. 138f the very bottom: one card from anywhere, tomorrow’s shelves, every subject.

133 Explore shelves, built on what Astute is for

SCOPO.md: five cards a day that leave you sharper, harder to fool and better at asking the right question, and a day is a mix of cards to read and cards to do. Only the shelves below “The ones that ask the most” change; everything above stays as in 131a. Each version bets on one way the shelves can serve that purpose. 133a every card says what you will do with it, and a filter splits reading from doing. 133b you commit to an answer on the shelf, before you open the card. 133c shelves built on one thinking move, met in different subjects. 133d shelves picked for you: cards that came back, a step above your level, your thinnest subject, the other side of an argument you took. It breaks the rule in themed_shelves.dart that shelves are the same for everybody. 133e a form for nine more of the nineteen themes the app rotates, with their titles from the app.

132 Explore shelves, refined: one signature per kind

Bigger cards, bigger questions, and one confident graphic per kind of shelf, drawn in a darker tone of the card’s own colour so it never fights the text: a struck-out quote for myths, a ruler of years for the past, the figure itself for numbers, two halves for a debate, a stamp for a place, a sun about to set for things to try before tonight, two overlapping circles for a paradox. 132a is the whole screen with every shelf scrolling sideways, as in the app; 132b puts the same signatures in different layouts.

131 Explore shelves: a shape for every kind of card

131a is the screen as it ships, rebuilt from the app’s code. Below Top of the week every shelf uses the same 158 × 172 card, so seven themes in a row read as one long shelf. In 131b–131f everything else stays as it is (colours, Fraunces questions, Figtree labels, radii, spacing, shelf titles). Only the shape of each shelf changes, so you can tell what kind of card a shelf holds before reading it. b–e start where the themed shelves begin; 131f is the whole screen with my recommended mix. Shelves scroll sideways as in the app.
